findings.title: The 30 s poll deadline is 4-20x longer than the lateness it was built for, and it holds the leg inside the window of the third race the implementer recorded as unfixed
findings.evidence: Ticket line: "the fix removes flakiness without weakening what the leg establishes." Measured recovery times, from the implementer's own report: unperturbed both polls converge on the FIRST sweep in 6-25 ms (clara_941-945); under `late_poison` at 1.5 s the refusal is counted after 4 sweeps / 1516 ms (clara_929); under `slow_settle` firm Q converges after 6 sweeps / 2774 ms (clara_928). Against that, `LEG4_DEADLINE_MS` is 30000 (packages/runtime/tests/intake-batch-e2e.mjs:145) and it governs BOTH loops separately, so the block can now spend 60 s in LEG 4. The implementer also measured that firm P's children reach `failed` on their own "inside 8 s" (clara_922, clara_927, clara_933) and that once they do, the belt correctly settles firm P's parent — which reds assertion 3 (`assert.equal(pFinal.state, "cancelling", ...)`, line 770). The file says so itself (line 133): "Keep it WELL under the few seconds firm P's children survive (measured: an 8000 ms delay let the World drive them to `failed` first, which is the OTHER defect, not this one)." The fix obeys that rule for the FAULT knob and breaks it for the DEADLINE. Net effect: in exactly the CI conditions #1027 exists for — a World too busy to converge in the first second — the P-loop now polls for up to 30 s through a window in which the third race is close to certain, and the gate reds on assertion 3 or at the deadline with P's children `failed`. That is the signature of CI job 105954490814, which the implementer's report states may have BEEN the third race all along.
findings.required_fix: Give the P-loop (and ideally the Q-loop) its own deadline inside the measured safe band — roughly 5 s covers the 1516 ms worst case with 3x margin and reds well before the 8 s at which P's children die — rather than one shared 30 s constant. If a 30 s deadline is deliberate, state in the file why a red at t+30 s is preferable to a red at t+5 s given that the intervening 25 s is the third race's window. File the third race as its own ticket either way (see summary).

findings.title: The refusal assertion polls a GLOBAL counter summed over up to 60 sweeps, so any unrelated parent's error satisfies "firm P's refusals are COUNTED"
findings.evidence: Ticket line: "The leg still proves that the poisoned firm's parent remains unfinished while the healthy firm's reaches its terminal state, with no assertion weakened or removed." The loop accumulates `pWatch.refusals += (sweep.batchCancelFailed ?? 0)` (intake-batch-e2e.mjs:699) and breaks on `>= 1`. `batchCancelFailed` is estate-wide, not per-parent: packages/runtime/lib/reconciler-batches.mjs:123-126 increments it in a catch-all — `} catch (err) { failed += 1; ...` — for ANY parent on the worklist whose fan-out throws for any reason. LEG 2's `bBatch` is still `cancelling` and therefore still on that worklist when LEG 4 runs (it claims a run on `bChildren[1]` at line 517 and never settles it), so the worklist is not firm P alone. The single-shot original had one chance to be satisfied by a stray error; the poll has up to sixty. The leg already computes the attributable signal and throws it away: `pWatch.blocked += (sweep.batchCancelBlocked ?? 0)` (line 700) — `batchCancelBlocked` is incremented only for a parent whose refusals are ALL CLR04 (reconciler-batches.mjs:114-116), which is exactly and only firm P's condition — and it is printed at line 708 but never asserted.
findings.required_fix: Require `pWatch.blocked >= 1` alongside the refusal count, or attribute the refusal to firm P directly (`clara.get_intake_batch(pBatch)` reports the same condition as `cancel_blocked`, per README line ~1398). The counters' meaning does not change, so this stays inside the ticket's "Out of scope: any change to the cancellation belt's own behaviour, counters or receipt shape."

findings.title: The new diagnostic rule misreads a genuinely broken belt as the unfixed third race — the implementer's own vacuity control proves it
findings.evidence: The ticket asks for a deadline that "fails with a message naming the firm, the parent and the state actually observed", and the fix goes further by writing a reading rule into the file (intake-batch-e2e.mjs:136-140): "If firm P's children are already `failed` there, this race is not what happened: the poisoned parent was declared done because its children died on their own under the World ... That is NOT fixed here — it is a separate defect." The same claim is repeated in packages/runtime/README.md ("What #1027 did NOT fix, and how to recognise it"). But the report's own vacuity control — clara_933, where `fanOutCancel` was deliberately broken so a CLR04 refusal is recorded as a SUCCESS — reds with precisely that census: `firm P (poisoned) parent=fbad1919-… state=cancelled children=[{"status":"failed",…}]`. So the documented signature of "a different defect, not addressed here" is also the signature of the one regression this assertion exists to catch. A reader following the rule would close a real belt regression as the known third race.
findings.required_fix: Either add a discriminator the census can carry (e.g. print each child's cancel receipt / refusal code, or `batchCancelBlocked` for firm P, which is >=1 under the real third race and 0 under a belt that records refusals as successes) or soften the rule to "consistent with, but does not establish" and say what does establish it.

findings.title: A permanent fault-injection harness was added to the shipped gate; the ticket asked only for convergence
findings.evidence: Nothing in #1027's Agent Brief asks for a retained fault knob; its Desired behaviour is confined to "The leg converges before it judges" and its Key interfaces name only the convergence helper, the belt receipt and the settle call. The diff adds `CLARA_P636_LEG4_FAULT` and `CLARA_P636_LEG4_FAULT_MS` (intake-batch-e2e.mjs:147-148) plus ~55 lines of comment and three live branches: `slow_settle` claims a run on each of firm Q's children BEFORE the cancel (line 638, changing the leg's own shape), `late_poison` defers `applyPoison()` behind a `sleep` (line 660), and `settleGateUntil`/`settleGateOpen()` sit on the settle path that runs on every poll (lines 714, 726). VERIFIED HARMLESS on the two axes that matter: both default inert (`LEG4_FAULT = process.env.CLARA_P636_LEG4_FAULT || ""`, and `settleGateUntil = 0` makes `settleGateOpen()` unconditionally true), and a repo-wide grep for `CLARA_P636_LEG4|CLARA_GATE_*` outside docs returns only intake-batch-e2e.mjs, the action, the README and the two world-gate scripts — no product path reads them. No product behaviour can change and nothing leaks.
findings.required_fix: None required for correctness. Decide deliberately whether the knob stays now that the evidence it produced is recorded in the report and the README; if it stays, that is a keep worth one line in the ticket's closing note rather than an unremarked addition.

findings.title: Firm P's cancellation decision was reordered to run after firm Q's, unasked and unremarked
findings.evidence: Before: `cancel_intake_batch(pAgent, pBatch)` then `cancel_intake_batch(Q.owner, qBatch)` then the membership removal. After: firm Q's cancel runs first and firm P's moved inside `applyPoison()` (intake-batch-e2e.mjs:648-653) alongside the removal. The leg's claim — "firm Q's batch, swept in the SAME belt call as firm P's poison" — still holds because both parents are `cancelling` before the first sweep on the default path, so this is not a defect. It is simply not something the ticket asked for and the implementer's report does not mention it.
findings.required_fix: None. Noted so the reordering is a known consequence of hoisting the poison into a callable for the fault path, not an accident.

findings.title: A child the World has already terminalised is recorded in the settle census as an error
findings.evidence: Ticket line: "A settlement that cannot be performed is surfaced rather than silently discarded." The implementation records `s.error = "no current task to settle at this poll"` (intake-batch-e2e.mjs:723) for a child with no `current_task_id`, and `s.settled` stays false forever for that child. That is the normal state of a child the World already drove terminal, but in the deadline message it prints beside genuine settle failures as `{"settled":false,"error":"no current task…"}`. The message AC exists to make a red diagnosable at a glance; this wording works against it.
findings.required_fix: Distinguish the two — e.g. a third state (`settled: "not-needed"` / `terminal-already`) or read the child's Work status into the census line — so a reader can tell "nothing to settle" from "settle refused".

findings.title: AC2's per-step measurement exists for 1 leg of 24; 21 legs are moved to a halved ceiling with no recorded figure at all
findings.evidence: Ticket line: "The chosen budget is justified by a recorded measurement of that step's peak memory across at least three runs, and the measurement method is written down." Counted myself by parsing .github/actions/db-live-gates/action.yml with the repo's own yaml: 7 steps, 24 `node` lines routed through `scripts/ci/world-gate.mjs`, 3 bare `node` lines (all `packages/db/scripts/{backup,restore-full,dr-verify}.mjs` in the DR step — not World-booting). Of those 24 legs, the README table records 3 runs for `intake-batch-e2e.mjs`, ONE run each for `intake-admission-e2e.mjs` (1.15 GiB) and `accrual-e2e.mjs` (0.43 GiB), and nothing for the other 21. The implementer states this plainly (report, "Anything unverified" #3: "21 of the 24 wired legs were not run under the budget"; README: "The other legs' peaks are recorded above only where they were measured"), so it is a disclosed partial, not a concealed one. What makes it more than bookkeeping is the one datapoint we have for an UNBOUNDED leg at this budget: `intake-batch-e2e.mjs` at 2048 with no in-process bound peaked at 1832 / 1969 MB occupancy and 1.97 / 2.11 GiB RSS — 98-105 % of the budget. 22 of the 24 legs have no in-process bound (only `intake-batch-e2e.mjs` and `interview-e2e.mjs` arm `startHeapBound()`), and none of them has ever been run at 2048. Whether that ceiling is safe for them is unverified in both directions.
findings.required_fix: Record the figures AC2 asks for, or record an explicit accepted deviation on #1026 before it closes. The cheap route: the Wave-B step already runs 20 of the 24 legs in one step, so one CI run of db-live-gates on this branch produces per-leg evidence — at minimum capture each step's success and any `::error::` annotation, and add the peak for the two or three heaviest legs. Do not close AC2 as met.

findings.title: Arming startHeapBound() inside the leg is what makes AC3's margin achievable, and its own cost is compared against the wrong baseline
findings.evidence: The ticket's Key interfaces name the action's per-step environment, the README's recorded figure and a shared launcher. Arming an in-process forced-collection bound INSIDE the gate is none of those; it is a change to what the leg does, not to the ceiling it runs under. It is also load-bearing for AC3: the implementer's own measurement is that "at 2048 with no in-process bound, occupancy runs to 1832-1969 MB of 2048 before every collection, so peak RSS lands at 98-105 % of the budget", i.e. AC3's "at least twenty five percent below the budget" is unreachable by budget alone. ON THE MARGIN ITSELF, AC3 IS MET by the recorded numbers of the final configuration: 0.79 / 0.91 / 0.93 GiB peak RSS and 657 / 717 / 795 MB peak occupancy against 2048 MB = 53-61 % below, and RSS >= old-space occupancy so the RSS figure is the conservative one. What the record obscures is the bound's price. README: "Wall clock is NOT better here (2:35-3:22 against 0:56-3:11 at the default ceiling)" — that compares budget+bound against the DEFAULT-ceiling band. The like-for-like pair on the same rig, isolating the bound, is the table's own rows: 2048-no-bound at 0:56 / 1:14 against 2048+bound at 2:00 / 2:17 / 2:51 — the bound roughly doubles the leg's wall clock. That matters here specifically because #1027 has just given the same leg 30 s convergence deadlines and because the third race the implementer recorded fires when the leg is SLOW (P's children reach `failed` "inside 8 s"). A second consequence to record: the leg's post-change peak figures are now a property of the 512 MB forced-collection threshold (packages/runtime/tests/heap-bound.mjs:63, collection via an in-process inspector `HeapProfiler.collectGarbage`), not of the runtime, so they are not comparable to any pre-change figure and any future review of the budget must hold the bound constant.
findings.required_fix: In packages/runtime/README.md's #1026 prose, compare the bound against 2048-no-bound (0:56 / 1:14 vs 2:00-2:51) rather than against the default-ceiling band, and say that the bound is what buys AC3's margin. State whether the doubled wall clock widens the third-race window in LEG 4, or mark that unverified. No change to the code is needed if both are recorded.

findings.title: The three world-provisioning commands do not go through the launcher
findings.evidence: Ticket line: "Every live-gates step that boots a durable World runs under an explicit, committed heap budget rather than the host default." Every e2e LEG is wrapped — I confirmed by YAML parse that no bare `node tests/` line remains. What is not wrapped is `pnpm --filter @clara/runtime exec bootstrap` at action.yml lines 93, 164 and 615, which resolves to `@workflow/world-postgres/bin/setup.js` (verified by reading packages/runtime/node_modules/.bin/bootstrap) — the command that provisions the durable World, and the one the step names after ("isolated DB + world bootstrap"). Short-lived DDL, and neither historical abort (jobs 105215992382, 106048901216) was in it, so this is a gap in coverage rather than a hole in the fix.
findings.required_fix: Either route the three `exec bootstrap` invocations through the launcher too, or add one line to the action's #1026 comment block saying the budget covers the e2e legs and deliberately not the world-provisioning step, with the reason.

findings.title: Nothing enforces the wiring — a new gate CAN still be added without a budget
findings.evidence: Ticket line (Key interfaces): "Any shared helper that launches these e2e processes should be the single place the budget is applied, so a new gate cannot be added without one." The launcher is that single place, but `scripts/ci/world-gate.selftest.mjs` tests only the launcher's own functions and spawned behaviour (I re-ran it: 12/12 PASS) — it never reads `.github/actions/db-live-gates/action.yml`. A contributor adding `node tests/new-leg.mjs` directly to the action gets no red; I re-ran `CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true pnpm lint` and it is exit 0 with no wiring check in the chain. The action's own comment is carefully worded around the gap — "A leg wired through that launcher cannot be added without a budget" (action.yml:30-32) — which is true but weaker than what the ticket asked for. The repo's established idiom is exactly this kind of guard in the lint chain (check-frozen-workflows.mjs, check-leaks.mjs, check-dead-citations.mjs).
findings.required_fix: Add a cell to world-gate.selftest.mjs that parses .github/actions/db-live-gates/action.yml and fails on any `node ` invocation of a `tests/` entry point that is not routed through world-gate.mjs. It is already in `pnpm lint`, so the guard costs nothing extra to run.

findings.title: CLARA_GATE_NODE is an unrequested, undocumented third knob on the launcher
findings.evidence: scripts/ci/world-gate.mjs:103 — `const nodeBin = env.CLARA_GATE_NODE || process.execPath;`. The launcher's own header documents `CLARA_GATE_STEP` and `CLARA_GATE_HEAP_MB` and says nothing about this one; the selftest does not cover it; nothing in the repo sets it (verified by grep — the only hits for `CLARA_GATE_*` outside docs are the action, the two world-gate scripts and the README). The ticket asked for a budget and an attributable death, not for a substitutable Node binary — and a wrapper whose whole job is "this process ran under this ceiling" is the last place to leave the interpreter swappable and unremarked. No product risk: the file is CI-only and reads no product path.
findings.required_fix: Drop it, or document it in the header beside the other two with the case it serves.

findings.title: The launcher path assumes $GITHUB_WORKSPACE is set
findings.evidence: All 24 invocations are `node "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/ci/world-gate.mjs" tests/<leg>.mjs`. Outside GitHub Actions the variable is empty and the path degrades to `/scripts/ci/world-gate.mjs`, which fails with a spawn error rather than a legible message. This only bites someone reproducing the action locally, which the repo's rig notes suggest does happen.
findings.required_fix: None required. If cheap, `${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-$PWD}` or one line in the action comment naming the assumption.

findings.title: A fix round landed in the worktree DURING this review; it addresses five of the six #1027 findings but introduces two new problems of the class #1027 exists to remove
findings.evidence: STATE OF THE SUBJECT: HEAD is still dd3d335dd (the fixed point of this review) and my findings above are all recorded against that commit. But `git status` now shows ` M packages/runtime/tests/intake-batch-e2e.mjs` — 176 insertions / 80 deletions, uncommitted — whose comments cite this review's ids verbatim ("review SPEC-1027-01", "-02", "-03", "-04", "-06", plus "review STD-3" from the Standards axis). It appeared between my reading of the diff and my writing of this file; I did not make it and I have not touched it. It syntax-checks (`node --check` clean). WHAT IT ADDRESSES: SPEC-1027-01 (one 30 s deadline split into P=5000 / Q=8000, each with its measured justification written in, total polling bounded at 13 s); SPEC-1027-02 (the P-loop now breaks on `refusals >= 1 && blocked >= 1`, asserts both, and adds a per-parent door assertion); SPEC-1027-03 (the census now prints `cancel_blocked`, `refusals` and `blocked`, and the reading rule is softened to "CONSISTENT WITH, but does not by itself establish"); SPEC-1027-04 (the knob is kept with the reason stated, and `LEG4_FAULT_MS` drops 6000 -> 1500 so a repro sits inside the new deadline); SPEC-1027-06 (the settle census gains a `state` field — not-attempted / settled / nothing-to-settle / held-by-fault / settle-refused — plus `work_status`). SPEC-1027-05 is untouched, which is correct: it asked for nothing. TWO NEW PROBLEMS, both in that uncommitted work, both verified against migration 0229 lines 1087-1095 which I read: (1) THE FIRM-Q CONTROL CANNOT FAIL. `assert.equal((await getBatch(Q.owner, qBatch)).cancel_blocked, null, "…while the healthy firm's stop was never blocked — the door tells the two apart")` runs after firm Q's parent has reached `cancelled`, and 0229 gates the whole derivation on `if b.state = 'cancelling' and b.cancel_requested_by is not null` — so a terminal parent returns null unconditionally, whatever the door thinks. The control asserts a constant and proves nothing about discrimination. (2) THE NEW DOOR ASSERTION IS AN UN-POLLED SINGLE-SHOT READ OF A FACT THE WORLD CAN INVALIDATE — the exact shape #1027 was written to delete. `assert.equal(pBlocked, "canceller_not_active")` reads once, after the P-loop; by the same 0229 gate it returns null the moment firm P's parent goes terminal, which is precisely the third race. So the third race now has a THIRD place to surface, and this one is the least legible of them: unlike assertion 3 below it, the door assertion's message carries no census (`got null` and nothing else). A related residual on the discriminator itself: because `cancel_blocked` depends only on the stored canceller's live membership and not on the belt, it reads the same under a belt regression as under the third race, so `blocked`/`refusals` plus the child census remain the only real discriminator — and a third race in which ALL of firm P's children are terminal before the first sweep produces `blocked=0, refusals=0`, which the rewritten rule tells the reader to call "a REGRESSION in the belt". The misdiagnosis is narrowed and inverted, not closed.
findings.required_fix: Before that fix round is committed: drop the vacuous firm-Q control or move it to a moment when firm Q's parent is still `cancelling` (it is a real control only there); give the new door assertion the same census tail that assertion 3 carries (`pTail`), or fold it into the polled loop rather than reading it once; and extend the reading rule to say that `blocked=0, refusals=0` WITH firm P's children already `failed` is the third race, not a belt regression. None of this changes my verdict on dd3d335dd, which is the commit under review.

summary: SPEC axis, 7b83b1c0d...dd3d335dd, two commits, two tickets. Verdict accept-with-fixes: 0 blockers, 3 major, 5 minor, 5 note. READ SPEC-META-01 FIRST: a fix round landed UNCOMMITTED in the worktree during this review, citing these finding ids; it addresses five of the six #1027 findings and introduces two new problems that should be caught before it commits. HEAD is still dd3d335dd and everything below is recorded against that commit. Nothing here is a reason to hold the branch, but two items should be settled before either ticket is closed as met. RE-RUN AND VERIFIED MYSELF: `node scripts/ci/world-gate.selftest.mjs` 12/12 PASS; `CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true pnpm lint` exit 0 with the new selftest in the chain; `node --check packages/runtime/tests/intake-batch-e2e.mjs` clean; a YAML parse of the action (7 steps, 24 launcher-wrapped node lines, 3 bare node lines all in the DR step and all `packages/db/scripts/*`, 3 unwrapped `exec bootstrap`). I did NOT run any World leg. #1027 CHECKS THE ORCHESTRATOR ASKED FOR: firm P's refusal is still asserted as counted — the loop breaks only on `refusals >= 1`, the deadline throws, and a redundant `assert.ok(pWatch.refusals >= 1)` follows, so it can never pass at 0 (but see SPEC-1027-02: the counter is estate-wide, not firm P's). Firm Q must still reach `cancelled` and nothing weaker — the loop breaks only on that string and asserts it after. A deadline names what was last observed — `leg4Diagnosis()` re-reads both parents' states and every child's Work status and current task at the moment of failure, plus the last receipt, the sweep count and the elapsed ms; the implementer quotes it verbatim from a real red. The polls cannot mask a real defect: if the belt never cancelled firm Q the block reds at 30 s with that census, and the implementer's deliberate vacuity control (fanOutCancel rewritten so a CLR04 refusal records as a success) did red, after 59 sweeps in 30.5 s. #1026 CHECKS: every World-booting e2e leg really does go through the launcher — 24 of 24, counted by YAML parse, none bare; the only unwrapped World-touching command is `exec bootstrap` (SPEC-1026-03). NODE_OPTIONS is appended, not replaced (`childEnv`, and a spawned selftest cell proves the child's heap_size_limit actually drops). The over-budget message fires on 134 / 137 / SIGABRT / SIGKILL and never on exit 0, 1 or 2 — the selftest's spawned positive control asserts an exit 1 passes through with no `::error::` at all. The 25 % margin criterion IS met by the recorded numbers: 0.79 / 0.91 / 0.93 GiB RSS and 657 / 717 / 795 MB occupancy against 2048 MB, i.e. 53-61 % below, with RSS the conservative measure — but only in the budget+bound configuration (SPEC-1026-02). Arming startHeapBound() does change what the leg measures: the post-change peaks are a property of the helper's 512 MB forced-collection threshold rather than of the runtime, so they are not comparable to pre-change figures, and the bound roughly doubles the leg's wall clock against the 2048-no-bound rows in the implementer's own table. ON THE RECORDED FOLLOW-UP (firm P's children driven terminal by the World before the belt sees them): it should be ITS OWN TICKET, not a blocker on this change. It predates this work, #1027's brief names only the two observations, the five-consecutive-run acceptance passed, and every failure mode is strictly more legible than the `actual: 'cancelling'` the two CI reds used to give. But it should be filed before this wave merges, for one concrete reason: the delivered 30 s deadline can still red the gate on exactly the CI signature #1027 was written to remove, and a shorter P-loop deadline inside the measured 1.5-8 s safe band would make that materially less likely (SPEC-1027-01).
